summary: Discovery to map CortexGate's integration needs for Redwood. CortexGate requires VPC-only connectivity, KMS-managed key control, SOC2 evidence, and per-tenant quotas. They plan to embed LLM features into a high-throughput customer chat product and need guidance on Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs. Agreed to a pilot using Dedicated capacity for baseline performance followed by security deep-dive.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-11
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Daniel (CTO CortexGate), Priya (Platform Eng), Marcus (SRE)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for taking time today, really excited to learn more about CortexGate's plans and how we can help with the onramp. Quick round robin?
[00:10] Daniel: Hi, I'm Daniel, CTO. We're building a multi-tenant conversational layer for B2B customers, latency sensitive, lots of small chats.
[00:18] Priya: Priya, platform engineering. I'll own the integration. We have strict networking, everything must go through a private VPC and we manage keys with Vault/KMS.
[00:26] Marcus: Marcus, SRE, mainly worried about quotas, burst capacity, and observability.
[00:31] Liam: Great, thanks. I'll tee up some questions about traffic shape and then walk through SDK and gateway options.

[01:00] Liam: Can you tell us the typical request profile? tokens, average prompt size, qps?
[01:08] Daniel: Most of our chats are short — average 60 to 120 tokens, about 30 to 70 qps now, spiky up to 300 qps during certain jobs. We're aiming to scale to sustained 200 qps.
[01:22] Priya: Also we have per-tenant rate limits and need to enforce them at the gateway level, not rely purely on provider-side quotas.

[02:10] Maya: Good context. There are three deployment options we usually discuss: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Private (VPC/on-prem). Given your VPC requirement and KMS, Private or Dedicated with VPC peering are common.
[02:26] Daniel: Clarify — Dedicated still goes through Redwood's control plane, right? We don't want our data in shared S3 buckets.
[02:32] Liam: Correct, Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools and data isolation; logs can be routed to your accounting, and Blob storage can be configured per-customer. For Private, the control plane is customer-owned and you can run the control plane on your VPC or on-prem.

[03:00] Marcus: What's the difference for observability? We need tracing into our APM, per-request token-level cost breakdown, and to attach request ids.
[03:10] Liam: We provide tracing hooks and a tracing header you pass through the SDK/gateway. There is an observability webhook and OpenTelemetry export. Note — sometimes the auto-parsed model labels can be a bit noisy in the transcript/downstream metrics.

[04:00] Priya: On SDKs — we currently use LangChain and LlamaIndex in our orchestration. How first-class are those integrations?
[04:08] Liam: We maintain an official Redwood SDK with LangChain adapters and example LlamaIndex connectors. We'll share the repo. The SDK supports streaming responses and function-calls. There are minor friction points: LangChain's retry semantics and Redwood's continuous batching need to be configured together to avoid duplicate tokens.
[04:30] Daniel: Is there a recommended pattern for the gateway? We want a proxy close to our services to handle per-tenant auth and quotas but minimize latency to Redwood endpoints.
[04:40] Maya: Common pattern is an edge gateway/proxy that enforces per-tenant quotas and auth, signs requests to Redwood, and optionally does prefix caching. Some customers run the gateway in the same VPC to reduce latency (and egress).

[06:00] Marcus: We have multi-region tenants — can Redwood route by region/latency or do we need separate instances?
[06:08] Liam: Routing can be policy-driven. You can pin tenants by region to a specific deployment (hosted region or Dedicated pool). If you need active-active, we recommend multi-region Dedicated pools or Private control plane with region-aware workers. Fallbacks to cheaper model variants are supported when capacity is constrained.

[07:15] Daniel: Quotas — we need both per-tenant and per-route rate limiting, and burst credits. Do you support token-based quotas?
[07:24] Liam: Yes. Redwood supports token-based quotas and per-route caps. On Dedicated you can set compute reservations plus burst buckets. The gateway typically enforces the initial per-tenant token budget and the Redwood side can be a second guardrail.

[08:00] Priya: Security — SOC2, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS integration. Also audit logs that we can push to our SIEM.
[08:08] Maya: We are SOC2 and provide attestations. For Private we integrate with your KMS/HSM; for Dedicated we support customer-managed keys and can stream audit logs to your S3 or syslog. We'll attach our security deck after the call.

[09:20] Marcus: Observability hooks — how do we get token-level latency and cost?
[09:28] Liam: We expose per-request token counts, model used, latency breakdowns, and cost estimates in the built-in console. We also provide a webhook for per-request events you can send into your pipeline, and OpenTelemetry spans for tracing. There's a small overhead when you enable token-level tagging — typically a few ms.

[11:10] Daniel: About the SDK: do you have code samples for LangChain retriever pipelines with LlamaIndex embeddings?
[11:18] Liam: Yes — sample shows embeddings -> persistent vector store -> reranker -> generator. We'll share a repo link (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/langchain-examples). Note: some model names in the readme are auto-generated and may not match the prod catalog exactly.

[12:45] Priya: If we run a pilot on Dedicated, how long to set up? We have strict network approvals.
[12:52] Maya: For Dedicated with VPC peering, typical onramp is 3-4 weeks once network approvals are in. Private can be longer depending on infra and on-prem constraints. We can do a short hosted pilot but that won't meet your VPC-only policy.

[14:20] Marcus: We need SLAs — and a rollback path for model regressions.
[14:26] Liam: Redwood has rollout policies: canary, A/B tests, automatic fallback. For Dedicated customers we can include an SLA for throughput/latency. For Private, SLA terms depend on the deployment agreement.

[16:00] Daniel: Performance — what's realistic for p99 for 120 token responses on Dedicated?
[16:10] Liam: On a well-tuned Dedicated pool with batching and KV cache, 90-150ms p50 and 300-450ms p99 depending on model size. If you use a smaller quantized variant you'll trade quality for latency. We'll provide benchmarks tailored to your workload as part of the pilot.

[18:30] Priya: Caching — can we do prefix-level cache at the gateway to avoid hitting the model for repeated prompts?
[18:36] Liam: Yes, prefix caching is supported. Gateway can implement a deterministic cache key. Redwood also has automatic KV cache for autoregressive decoding which reduces repeated compute for similar prefixes. Note: cache invalidation and multi-tenant isolation are important to design carefully.

[20:00] Marcus: On costing — we need predictable unit economics. How do we get token breakdowns?
[20:08] Maya: The console provides token-level billing. For Dedicated, you also get committed capacity pricing which smooths unit costs. Redwood Optimize suggests quantization and batching settings to reduce cost per token based on observed workload.

[22:10] Daniel: Integrations — can we use our existing ingress (kong/envoy) as gateway or do you recommend the Redwood edge?
[22:18] Liam: You can use Kong/Envoy as the gateway. We provide a lightweight SDK for signing and telemetry that plugs into Envoy's Lua/filters or a sidecar. Some customers prefer a Redwood-managed edge for simplicity but it's optional.

[24:00] Priya: On observability again, how do retries look? We need idempotency keys so we can reconcile retries in our logs.
[24:08] Liam: SDK supports idempotency/request-id header. We recommend wiring that into your APM. Beware LangChain's internal retries — you should disable or align them with your gateway retry policy to avoid duplicate charges.

[26:40] Marcus: Are there known quirks with LlamaIndex connectors and vector stores?
[26:48] Liam: LlamaIndex versions sometimes have breaking changes. Our sample repo pins versions. For vector stores we support standard embeddings output and provide recommended size/thresholds for nearest neighbor recall vs latency.

[29:00] Daniel: Could you summarize the recommended pilot approach?
[29:06] Maya: Yes. Short version: 1-week Dedicated pilot with a reserved pool sized for 50 qps sustained with burst headroom to 200 qps. We'll run your LangChain/LlamaIndex pipeline against a synthetic corpus, capture p50/p99 latency and token cost, and export traces to your APM. Security deep-dive happens in parallel.

[31:20] Priya: For the pilot we need a sample Helm chart or Terraform snippets to wire VPC peering and route tables.
[31:28] Liam: We'll provide a starter repo with Terraform snippets for VPC peering, security group examples, and Envoy sidecar config.

[33:00] Daniel: Any blockers you see?
[33:06] Liam: Network approvals and KMS policy are the main ones. Also quirk: if you insist on on-prem HSMs, Private deployment will need a longer lead time.

[34:40] Maya: Pricing note — we will send both per-token hosted and committed capacity Dedicated pricing. For enterprise terms we'll include security annex (SOC2, encryption, audit log flow).

[36:50] Marcus: How do you handle tenant-level observability in the console? Can we hide tokens for some tenants?
[36:58] Liam: You can filter in the console by tenant and set RBAC so only certain roles see cost. We can also push raw events to your S3 if you want to build your own dashboards.

[38:30] Daniel: Competitors question — some of our folks asked about Anthropic/Vertex. Are there model parity concerns?
[38:38] Maya: We can host a variety of open and verified models. The question is less about the model provider and more about serving economics and controls. Redwood focuses on predictable serving and observability which is our differentiator.

[40:50] Priya: Example resources to share?
[40:56] Maya: We'll share: 1) Hosted/Dedicated/Private comparison one-pager, 2) LangChain + LlamaIndex example repo, 3) Security deck and SOC2 attestation link, 4) Terraform/VPC peering snippets. Links: https://redwood.ai/onramp (deck), https://github.com/redwood-inference/langchain-examples (repo).

[42:30] Daniel: Sounds good. If pilot looks good, we'll discuss Dedicated commit.

[43:00] Maya: Next steps recap: I'll send pricing and security docs; Liam will push sample code; Priya will share network constraints; Daniel will confirm pilot stakeholders. We'll aim for security deep-dive next week.
[43:24] Daniel: Yep, thanks all.
[43:28] Marcus: Thanks, appreciated.
[43:31] Liam: Thanks everyone, talk soon.
[43:45] End call.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-hearings of product names (e.g., "Redwood dedicate" instead of "Redwood Dedicated") and model labels.
